notes: kb/Work PB5373 class 4, decided 2026-11-12. §1985:IX.1.3.4 GR6 (Implementor Defined): "The input-output statement was unsuccessfully executed as the result of a condition that is specified by the implementor", with "If more than one value applies, the implementor determines which of the applicable values to place in the I-O status". The antecedent is the implementor's to define and WiseOwl defines it: docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-110 specifies the 9x values ('90' the LINAGE value violation, which no indexed file reaches, and '91' a record character with no byte image in the file's coded character set, which an indexed WRITE or REWRITE reaches) and DOC-A.1-104 the order in which the applicable values are chosen. The witness is an 85 program that WRITEs to an INDEXED file a record holding U+20AC (IX-EURO=91, the record is not stored: a READ of its key is 23) and then U+00E9 (IX-E=00, READ gives the data), expected from the determination, not copied from a run; the unit test drives the same indexed refusal at the connector. IndexedConnector's write path asks FileConnector.RecordHasCharacterWithoutByteImage before the key rules and answers FileStatusCode.CharacterWithoutByteImage.

next.reason: 1985: "unsuccessfully executed as the result of a condition that is specified by the implementor. ... If more than one value applies, the implementor determines"; 2023: "An implementor-defined condition exists. This condition shall not duplicate any other condition specified by another I-O status value.". Both define the implementor-defined 9x status. 2023 forbids it duplicating other status conditions, and no candidate keeps the implementor's choice when several values apply.
